elements.element: No minimum purchase commitment applies to Customer.
elements.evidence: The operative clause expressly states that “Customer has no minimum purchase ... commitment.”

elements.element: No minimum volume commitment applies to Customer.
elements.evidence: The operative clause expressly states that Customer has no “volume commitment.”

elements.element: Customer pays fees only for actual usage or Services it orders.
elements.evidence: The operative clause states that Customer “pays only for usage or ordered Services.”

elements.element: Any commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: No commitment exists under the operative clause, so the condition for imposing a commitment duration is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Customer may reduce any commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: No commitment exists to be reduced, so the condition requiring a reduction right is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Any commitment shortfall is resolved through a true-up.
elements.evidence: Because the operative clause imposes no commitment, no commitment shortfall can arise and the true-up condition is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: No penalty applies to a commitment shortfall.
elements.evidence: The operative clause creates neither a commitment nor a shortfall remedy or penalty.

result.reason: The redline cleanly replaces the three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay obligation with the preferred position: no purchase or volume commitment and payment only for usage or ordered Services. It makes no unrelated operative changes. The fallback protections are also satisfied as protective ceilings because no commitment or resulting shortfall exists, although the fallback mechanics are not affirmatively implemented.
